description:
Welcome to CosmoFlux! We are a passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge.
​Our mission is to revive the forgotten stories of NASA's historic gear, rovers, and probes left on the Moon, Mars, and deep space. We aim to create an engaging, interactive, and educational storytelling experience that inspires school-age students and space enthusiasts.
summary: Team CosmoFlux presents 'Echoes in the Dust', a bilingual web application concept designed to revive historical space archives through interactive, gamified learning. The project addresses the problem of space history being trapped in static, complex archives by transforming them into accessible, engaging digital experiences. It features four interactive stations—collecting moon rocks with Apollo 17, wiping dust off Opportunity, flying Ingenuity, and tuning Voyager's signal—making space science closer to global and Arabic-speaking communities.
details:
'Echoes in the Dust' is a lightweight, bilingual (Arabic/English) web application built to make space exploration interactive and educational.
- What it does: Offers four distinct stations representing legendary missions (Apollo 17, Opportunity, Ingenuity, and Voyager), allowing users to experience historical space operations through mini-interactions.
- How it works: Users navigate a clean, responsive interface, select a mission, and engage with interactive elements simulating real space challenges (such as telemetry analysis and surface exploration).
- Tools & Technologies: Modern web development stack (HTML/CSS/JavaScript/React and Vercel for deployment).
- Working Features: Fully functional web app interface with active interactive stations and bilingual support.
- Limitations & Future Plans: Current version serves as an interactive conceptual pilot; future plans include expanding telemetry datasets and adding more historical missions.
